questions.stem: A student has to copy out this sentence and fill the blank with the right relative pronoun: Arenla took Sentila to the riverbank ________ the grey and red clay was found. (A) which (B) when (C) whose (D) where

evidence: Arenla took Sentila to the riverbank where the grey and red clay was found.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is opening a pottery workshop and a weaving centre and asks every student to choose one. Write a formal letter of 100 words to the head teacher giving your choice and the reasons for it.

markingPoints.description: Format: the letter is laid out correctly, with a heading, a salutation, the body and a closing.
Content: states clearly that the pottery workshop has been chosen.
Content: gives reasons drawn from the craft itself, such as digging, carrying, pounding, shaping and firing the pots.
Content: accepts the honest difficulties, that a batch takes months of labour and the reward is only a pittance.
Organisation and expression: the reasons are arranged in order, with correct spelling, punctuation and expression.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
The Pottery Workshop
Respected Sir/Madam,
I write to inform you of my choice. I have chosen the pottery workshop.
The work appeals to me because it is a skill that has been handed down from generation to generation and has stood for the tradition and history of our people. I know that the clay must be dug from the riverbank, carried uphill, pounded inside bamboo cylinders and shaped with a spatula, and that over firing or under firing will ruin a whole batch.
I accept that the reward is only a pittance.
Yours obediently,
[Your Name]

evidence: was her duty to teach her daughter the skill that was handed down from generation to generation.
firing or under firing would ruin the entire batch.
Also, the time spent on weaving one shawl is much less and the return is handsome.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: You have to speak in the school assembly to new students on why a traditional craft must not be allowed to die out. Write a speech of 100 words that opens with a greeting and closes with a thank-you.

markingPoints.description: Format: a speech with a greeting at the start and a thank-you at the end.
Content: describes the stages of the craft, that the clay is carried uphill, pounded in bamboo cylinders, shaped with a spatula, dried in the sun and fired in a kiln.
Content: explains the worth of the skill, that it catered to the needs of the people and symbolised their tradition and history.
Content: shows that the skill belonged to no individual and that experts were obliged to pass it on.
Organisation and expression: clear order, a suitable register for an assembly, and correct spelling and punctuation.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Honourable Principal, teachers and dear friends,
Our village had expert potters whose skill passed from generation to generation. The clay came from a riverbank and had to be carried uphill, then pounded inside bamboo cylinders before it could be shaped with a spatula. The pots were dried in the sun and fired in a kiln, where over firing or under firing would ruin the whole batch. Even so, the skill fed the people and stood for their tradition and history. It belonged to no individual, and every expert was obliged to pass it on. So do not turn away from a craft for its small reward. Learn it, and pass it on.
Thank you.

evidence: skills such as pot making, which not only catered to the needs of the people but also symbolised the tradition and history of the people, did not ‘belong’ to any individual.
experts were obliged to pass on their skills not only to their own children but also to anyone who wished to learn
out a batch of pots after so much labour. And the reward? A few rupees.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Another classmate wants to know how Onula helped Sentila; describe her part in about 50 words.

markingPoints.description: Onula had heard of the discord in Sentila’s family and resolved to help the girl in every possible way.
Seeing that Sentila was too tense for the clay to yield the right shape, she fashioned a beautiful pot and asked her to try again.
She pointed out that the mouth of the pot was wrong and sent Sentila to watch her mother shape it, so she mastered the rim.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Onula had heard of the discord in Sentila’s family and resolved to help her. When she saw that Sentila failed because she was too tense, she fashioned a beautiful pot and asked her to try again, and Sentila succeeded. Onula then told her the mouth of the pot was wrong and advised her to watch her mother shape it next time, and Sentila did.

evidence: She had heard of the discord in Sentila’s family and resolved to help the girl in every possible way.
She watched Sentila’s clumsy efforts to make a pot and noticed that Sentila was too tense.
When you work with your mother next time, watch her carefully when she is shaping the mouth of the pot.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A student asks why the village elders felt that pot making should not stay within one family; answer in about 50 words.

markingPoints.description: They were worried that if all pot makers followed suit, then there would be no expert potters to take their place.
The skill catered to the needs of the people and symbolised their tradition and history, so it did not belong to any individual.
Arenla had a duty to teach the skill handed down from generation to generation, and experts were obliged to pass it on to anyone who wished to learn.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The elders feared that if pot makers stopped teaching, no expert would be left to take their place. Pot making served the needs of the people and stood for their tradition and history, so it belonged to no individual. They told Mesoba that Arenla had a duty to pass on the skill handed down through generations, and that experts must teach anyone who wished to learn.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: In about 120 words, trace in steps the stages by which Sentila became a skilled pot maker, naming the person who helped her at each stage.

markingPoints.description: Sentila watched the expert potters and saw the clay mixed, pounded and shaped with a spatula held in the right hand.
Arenla took her to the riverbank and taught her to dig the clay with a dao, soak it in the trough and pound it in a bamboo cylinder.
Sentila could turn the clay into malleable dough but could not hold or shape the lump, and almost a year of practice taught her nothing.
In the girls’ dormitory Onula saw that she was too tense, made a perfect pot and asked her to try again, and Sentila created a beautiful pot.
Onula told her to watch her mother shaping the mouth, and Sentila learned how a strip of elongated dough was added to make the rim.
When Arenla was unwell and left her to work, Sentila made pot after pot and fell only one short of her mother’s tally.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Sentila watched the expert potters while Arenla was in the fields, learning how the clay was mixed, pounded and shaped with a spatula.
2. Arenla took her to the riverbank and taught her to dig the clay with a dao, soak it in the trough and pound it in a bamboo cylinder.
3. Sentila could turn the clay into dough but could not shape the lump, and a year of practice taught her nothing.
4. The next year, in a girls’ dormitory, Onula found her too tense, made a perfect pot and asked her to try again.
5. Onula sent her to watch her mother shape the mouth and rim.
6. When Arenla was unwell and left her to work, Sentila made pot after pot and fell only one short of her mother’s tally.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: In about 120 words, compare weaving with pot making on the grounds Arenla gave for preferring weaving.

markingPoints.description: Weaving lets Sentila make much more money besides providing enough cloth for the family.
Weaving is not messy like pot making and can be done indoors in all seasons.
The time spent on weaving one shawl is much less and the return is handsome.
Pot making needs clay from a riverbank sixteen kilometres away.
She had to climb down a sheer drop and carry the heavy load uphill to the village, and her back ached from it.
Pounding the stubborn clay inside bamboo cylinders was tedious, and a batch took months of labour for a reward of a few rupees.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Weaving, Arenla said, lets Sentila make much more money besides providing enough cloth for the family.
2. Weaving is not messy like pot making and can be done indoors in all seasons.
3. The time spent on weaving one shawl is much less and the return is handsome.
4. Pot making, by contrast, needs clay from a riverbank sixteen kilometres away, reached by climbing down a sheer drop.
5. The heavy load then had to be carried uphill to the village, and her back ached from it.
6. Pounding the stubborn clay inside bamboo cylinders was tedious, and a batch took months of labour for a reward of a few rupees.
